title: Continuity Sentinel & Loss-Tolerant Resequencing for Event Streams
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: clients experience partial transcripts and hard-to-reconcile state when long-running SSE responses are interrupted and retried. Existing heuristics rely on resume tokens tied to individual fragments; this leaves corner cases where small-loss bursts (network flaps, proxy resets) cause duplicate function calls or truncated structured outputs. Goal: design and implement a server+client side pattern that provides an explicit continuity sentinel and a loss-tolerant resequencing layer so clients can safely reattach mid-stream without risking duplicate tool/function calls or corrupting structured outputs. Scope: server-side sentinel emission, lightweight fragment headers (sequence anchor, semantic boundary hints, optional checksum), client-side resequencer with dedupe rules, backoff/lease semantics for ephemeral resume tokens, and end-to-end integration tests and SDK changes (Node/Python). Out of scope for this ticket: full persistent server-side chunk catalog for multi-day replay (future follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Server emits a continuity sentinel every N tokens with a stable sequence anchor and optional semantic boundary flag
Client SDKs can reattach and resume from the last seen anchor without re-delivering function/tool calls in >95% simulated packet-loss scenarios
Structured outputs (JSONL / function json payloads) are preserved without truncation or duplicate invocations across reconnects in our integration harness
Automated E2E tests covering network partitions, proxy 502/504s, and transient TCP resets pass in CI
Design doc and RFC reviewed and approved by Platform and SDK leads
Backward compatibility: servers accept older clients and expose sentinel metadata in a way that does not break tokenized streaming consumers
